opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require owning the system, which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training may have at most read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: There is conflicting information about Douglas Salinas (E045). HR states he is a full-time Engineer (which would allow write), but Security states his records show he is a contractor with only basic security training, which caps access at read for Payroll. Because the evidence conflicts and granting write would violate policy if the contractor classification is correct, I apply the more restrictive maximum and grant read. This is within policy under either classification and never exceeds the requested level.
